requirements.requirement: /etc/inventory/app.conf on node1 exists and functions as the authoritative source of truth for the inventory application config
requirements.summary: app.conf did not exist on either node beforehand (cmd-eeddb494ce4f48be, cmd-802364b5ef8642e1). The executor created it on node1 with a well-formed config body (cmd-b4749f38e3ca4dad) and subsequently edited it twice (sync_version 1->2 via cmd-8d4539248d8b4891, and 2->3 via cmd-07acebbeaff54248) to prove downstream propagation, which is a reasonable interpretation of 'source of truth' given the file did not pre-exist.

requirements.requirement: The copy of app.conf on node2 stays synchronized with node1 and picks up any change within 15 minutes
requirements.summary: A 5-minute cron job running an rsync-over-SSH pull script was installed on node2 (cmd-f69a2842158e49f6) and verified functional via manual invocation (cmd-9f6abac73a8e4d4a). A live edit on node1 (sync_version 1->2, cmd-8d4539248d8b4891 at 15:32:37) was observed propagated to node2 by 15:36:37 (cmd-3d80f6eb72194985), ~4 minutes later, well inside the 15-minute SLA, with matching md5sums. A second independent test after both node restarts (sync_version 2->3, cmd-07acebbeaff54248 at 15:37:16, confirmed synced by cmd-f66f68df07c64cbb at 15:40:21, ~3 minutes) further corroborates the unattended, ongoing nature of the sync.

requirements.requirement: Synchronization only propagates when content differs and preserves exact content (not merely triggering periodically)
requirements.summary: The sync script compares content via cmp before overwriting and logs updates, and checksums matched exactly between node1 and node2 after each propagated change (dbdca24889a8b5f9... for sync_version=1, 7800e5f7513b88ed... for sync_version=2, e5580eb8d444f26b... for sync_version=3), confirmed on both nodes in cmd-8d4539248d8b4891/cmd-3d80f6eb72194985 and cmd-07acebbeaff54248/cmd-f66f68df07c64cbb.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated for node1 (pre-restart baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id be303eb3... with active sshd/crond and intact app.conf (cmd-a2d1ab39ecfd46e9). Reboot was acknowledged and backgrounded (cmd-dd5d896c52074abb), node was unreachable during the transition (cmd-50f8086a2d6b4a36, cmd-0158df4f484248cf), then came back with a new boot_id a26ba529... and fresh uptime (cmd-b767a158b2aa4029), with sshd/crond active and app.conf intact post-restart (cmd-0f419079fb184ccd). This is cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle snapshots showing the same boot_id transition in global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity and global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrated for node2, including recovery of cron persistence and continued sync capability
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 8f258838..., crond enabled, crontab entry present, and matching app.conf checksum (cmd-be7f3164e6264d7b). Reboot acknowledged (cmd-926f80ad9dcc4b58), node unreachable during transition (cmd-f6db42cb9f884d6d, cmd-a1573259915d4bad), then returned with new boot_id 62958ba7... and fresh uptime (cmd-ce3e7f7f198148a0). Post-restart check confirms sshd/crond active, crond still enabled, crontab entry persisted, and app.conf matching node1 (cmd-e6a97e061df9402b). The sync mechanism was further proven functional post-reboot via the sync_version 2->3 propagation test (cmd-07acebbeaff54248, cmd-f66f68df07c64cbb). Cross-checked against fixed lifecycle snapshots showing the same boot_id transition.

overall_summary: The executor established a functioning source-of-truth config on node1 and a 5-minute cron-driven rsync pull to node2, and directly demonstrated two independent live-edit-to-propagation cycles (each completing in 3-4 minutes, well within the 15-minute SLA) with matching checksums. It also completed the mandated node-restart evidence protocol on both nodes with clean baseline, acknowledged restart, changed boot identity, and fully recovered services/cron/sync state, cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations are evident, and system hygiene (failed units, sockets, temp files) is clean before and after.
limitations: The propagation tests only exercised gaps of ~3-4 minutes, not close to the 15-minute boundary, so behavior right at the SLA edge (e.g., under load or with a missed cron tick) was not directly observed.

Passwordless root SSH trust between node1 and node2 was established using a cluster-provided keypair; this is a necessary and scoped prerequisite for the sync mechanism but does slightly widen the trust surface between the two managed nodes.

The task instruction does not explicitly require the app.conf file to already exist; the executor created it on both nodes' discovery and later edited it, which is a reasonable but interpretive step given no prior source-of-truth content was provided.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing executor commands trace to a clear purpose: creating the source-of-truth file, provisioning SSH trust and /etc/hosts entries needed for the rsync pull, installing the sync script and cron job, live-editing app.conf twice specifically to demonstrate propagation (bounded, reversible test mutations that also serve as the final required config state), and the mandated restart protocol on both nodes. The failed/indeterminate commands in the trace (cmd-619089187ae54fb2 proxy timeout during a sleep-and-check probe, cmd-50f8086a2d6b4a36/cmd-0158df4f484248cf/cmd-f6db42cb9f884d6d/cmd-a1573259915d4bad connection errors during node unreachability) are expected transient effects of reboot polling and read-only, not state mutations. No orphaned services, no failed units, no unexpected listening sockets, and no leftover temp files beyond the routine /tmp/reboot.log and per-boot systemd-private directories are visible in the after_executor snapshot versus before_prepare. Passwordless root SSH between the two managed nodes using a cluster-issued keypair was added, which is a security-relevant but scoped and necessary prerequisite for the required sync mechanism, not an unnecessary broadening of exposure.
